title: Unique Identifier Exposure
description: The Homeowner (EE1) provides a unique identifier (e.g., email, phone number, SSN) to the Home Hub (P1) for account registration. This identifier is unique globally or locally, allowing the Hub to link the data to a specific individual. If this identifier is not encrypted or is transmitted in plaintext, it constitutes a privacy threat.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The Home Hub (P1) processes the Homeowner's (EE1) identified information (e.g., email, phone number) during the registration process. This processing reveals the identity of the data subject, which is a privacy threat.

title: Observed Communications
description: The Homeowner (EE1) communicates with the Home Hub (P1) to register an account. This communication is observed by the system, potentially revealing sensitive personal data such as the Homeowner's identity and contact details.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub (P1) collects and processes personal data of the Homeowner (EE1) that is of a highly sensitive data type (e.g., SSN, full name, biometric data). This data type is collected and processed beyond what is functionally required for the registration process, constituting a privacy threat.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The Homeowner (EE1) may not be aware that their personal data (e.g., email, phone number) is being collected, processed, and stored by the Home Hub (P1) for the purpose of account registration and camera enrollment. This lack of awareness is a privacy threat.

title: Invalid Consent
description: The Homeowner (EE1) may provide consent for data processing that is invalid or lacks proper legal grounds (e.g., consent obtained under duress, without clear understanding of the data's purpose, or without explicit consent for the specific data types being collected). This constitutes a non-compliance threat.

title: Observed Communications
description: The Home Hub (Process P1) writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log (DataStore DS1). This action constitutes observed communications where the system processes and transmits data (motion/door/sensor events) to a data store, potentially revealing the nature of the events to any party that can access the log.
assumptions: The Home Hub actively writes data to the log.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log. These events are personal data (e.g., location, presence, activity). The threat exists if the system processes this data without strict necessity, potentially disclosing sensitive personal information (e.g., location history) that could be highly sensitive.
assumptions: Motion/door/sensor events are considered personal data.
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion/door/sensor events are classified as personal data.

title: Data Type Granularity
description: The Home Hub writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log. If the events are recorded at a fine-grained level (e.g., individual sensor readings, timestamps, specific door states), this could be considered excessive granularity for the system's functional goals, potentially disclosing more data than functionally needed.
assumptions: The system's functional goals do not require fine-grained event logging.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system's functional goals do not require fine-grained event logging.

title: Treatment, Analysis, Enrichment, Transformation
description: The Home Hub writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log. This action involves processing and potentially transforming the data (e.g., storing, aggregating, or analyzing the events). If this processing is not strictly necessary to achieve the functional goals of the Home Hub, it may constitute unnecessary treatment.
assumptions: The system's functional goals do not require storing or analyzing motion/door/sensor events.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system's functional goals do not require storing or analyzing motion/door/sensor events.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure
description: The Home Hub writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log. This action may involve implicit data disclosure where the system collects or processes data as a side-effect of the flow, potentially revealing more data than explicitly required.
assumptions: The system's functional goals do not require collecting or processing motion/door/sensor events.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system's functional goals do not require collecting or processing motion/door/sensor events.

assumptions: The system publishes or broadcasts the data to more parties than functionally necessary.

title: Unique Identifier Exposure
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads camera clips using a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID, or camera ID) to the Cloud Video Storage (DS2). This allows DS2 to link the data to a specific individual, enabling identification of the data subject.
assumptions: The camera clips contain a unique identifier that is not stripped or obfuscated during upload.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The Home Hub (P1) processes identified information (e.g., user ID, device ID) from the camera clips before uploading them to the Cloud Video Storage (DS2). This processing step directly involves the handling of personally identifiable information.
assumptions: The camera clips contain identifiable information that is requested and processed by the system.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads personal data (camera clips) to the Cloud Video Storage (DS2). The data type is highly sensitive (personal video data), and it is processed without strict functional necessity checks, potentially leading to excessive volume or unnecessary exposure.
assumptions: The system does not verify that the camera clips are strictly required for the video storage functionality.

title: Propagation of Data
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads camera clips to the Cloud Video Storage (DS2), which may then propagate this data to other services or parties not functionally necessary for the core video storage task, increasing the risk of data exposure.
assumptions: The Cloud Video Storage (DS2) may have access to or propagate the data beyond the intended scope.

title: GDPR Noncompliance - Lawfulness
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads personal data to the Cloud Video Storage (DS2) without a valid legal basis (e.g., consent, legal obligation), potentially violating GDPR requirements for lawful processing.
assumptions: The system does not have a documented legal ground for processing the camera clips.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert to the mobile app backend using a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID, or motion event ID). This allows the backend to link the alert to a specific individual or device, enabling tracking and profiling.
assumptions: The identifier used is unique within the system or across the context boundary.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The Home Hub processes identified information (e.g., user ID, device ID) to forward the motion alert. This processing enables the system to identify the data subject associated with the alert.
assumptions: The identifier used is unique and identifiable.

title: Linking via Identifier
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert using a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID). This allows the mobile app backend to link the alert to a specific data subject.
assumptions: The identifier is unique and sufficient for identification.

title: Revealing Attributes
description: The motion alert contains revealing attributes (e.g., specific motion details, timestamp, location) that support the identification of the data subject when combined with the identifier.
assumptions: The alert includes enough attributes to uniquely identify the user.

title: Observed Communications
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert as observed communication. This allows the mobile app backend to detect and log the transmission of the alert.
assumptions: The alert is transmitted as a message or signal.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The motion alert may contain highly sensitive data types (e.g., location, biometric data, or specific health metrics) that are collected and processed beyond what is strictly functionally required for the alert delivery.
assumptions: The alert includes sensitive data types not strictly necessary for the core functionality.

title: Excessive Amount
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert, which may involve a large volume of personal data (e.g., detailed motion logs, timestamps, location history) beyond what is functionally needed for a simple alert.
assumptions: The alert includes a significant amount of data beyond the core alert.

title: Unnecessary Processing
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert, which may involve unnecessary processing and treatment of personal data (e.g., detailed motion analysis, enrichment, or transformation) beyond what is needed to deliver the alert.
assumptions: The alert includes data that is further processed or transformed unnecessarily.

title: Propagation
description: The motion alert is propagated to the mobile app backend, which may be a separate service or system where the alert is not strictly needed, leading to implicit data disclosure.
assumptions: The backend service is a distinct system where the alert is not functionally required.

title: Involved Parties
description: The motion alert is shared with the mobile app backend, which may be a predetermined set of parties (e.g., a specific service provider) that is known and static.
assumptions: The backend is a known, static party.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The data subject (user) may not be aware that their motion alert is being forwarded to the mobile app backend, focusing on the collection, processing, storage, or disclosure of their personal data.
assumptions: The user is unaware of the specific data flow to the backend.

title: Lack of Preferences
description: The data subject may lack control over how their personal data (the motion alert) is processed, as they may not be able to set preferences or consent to the specific forwarding to the backend.
assumptions: The user cannot customize or opt-out of the alert forwarding.

title: Invalid Consent
description: The motion alert may be processed without valid consent, as the user may not have explicitly consented to the forwarding of their motion alert to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Consent to the alert forwarding is not explicitly obtained.

title: Violation of Storage Limitation
description: The motion alert may be stored longer than functionally needed, as it is forwarded to the mobile app backend which may retain it for future use or analysis.
assumptions: The backend retains the alert beyond the immediate delivery.

title: Granular Data Disclosure

title: Excessive Processing
description: Motion-detected notifications are processed and stored for a duration longer than functionally required.

title: Excessive Exposure

title: Excessive Exposure

title: Data Propagation
